title: Bloodline arm: one NON-Qwen LLM alone vs the same 4-member committee
author: mac-codex
origin: equal-budget-003 closed the BUDGET axis and said so in as many words: 'A and A' are both Qwen3. So the correct sentence is "a Qwen3-8B beat this committee", not "a big model beat this committee". A different-bloodline big model at equal weight is still unrun.' This run is that arm. The committee is adopted verbatim from 002; nothing else moves.

this_is_the_bloodline_arm_not_a_new_expe.what_moves: arm A only: Qwen3-8B (4.682 GiB, Q4_K_M) -> Yi-1.5-9B-Q4_K_M, a different lineage, reached over LAN
this_is_the_bloodline_arm_not_a_new_expe.what_is_held_frozen: arm B is adopted verbatim from assets/votes/equal-budget-002.raw.json via --reuse-arm-b; the tool refuses the donor unless suite, row count and member URLs match one for one
this_is_the_bloodline_arm_not_a_new_expe.why_holding_it_matters: re-harvesting the held arm would re-roll it (a timeout, a sampler decision on the second pass), and a between-runs delta would then be read as a between-arms delta

host.note: arm A is the first arm in this series scored ACROSS A LAN BOUNDARY; see declared_limits.latency_is_not_comparable

arm_a.role: one NON-Qwen LLM, alone, on the committee budget
arm_a.url_source: win root /nodes, read immediately before this run; stem ports rotate every restart and must never be cached
arm_a.weight_unverified_reason: win exposes no gguf file size over /nodes, the stem /health, or llama-server /props (all four probed 2026-10-19 07:0x; only checkpoint aliases come back). The mac therefore CANNOT claim this arm is at equal weight. Closing it needs one command on win: Get-Item D:\pando-models\*.gguf | Select-Object Name,Length
arm_a.no_new_model_loaded: win-yi-9b was already resident as a civilization member; this run started zero new model servers. Compare 003, which had to unload and reload the mac's 8B for ~15 minutes.

arm_b.role: the same committee, its votes taken from 002 rather than re-asked
arm_b.note: 8767 and 8770 are NOT listening right now. That is deliberate and harmless: --reuse-arm-b re-reads the stored votes, it does not re-ask the members. The tool refuses the donor if the member URL list differs by even one entry.

decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run.let d: (rows where arm A is right and arm B wrong) - (rows where arm B is right and arm A wrong), on rows both answered
decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run.d >= 0 means: this foreign-bloodline model is NOT better than the committee on these rows
decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run.d < 0 and |d| > 1.96*SE: the committee is ahead of THIS foreign model beyond noise on these rows
decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run.otherwise: inconclusive at this n; no claim either way

declared_limits.budget_axis_not_closed_by_this_run: the pre-registered control was 'a non-Qwen big model at equal weight'. Weight is unverified for arm A, so this run closes the BLOODLINE axis (a different lineage was actually measured on the identical rows) but leaves the equal-weight claim open. Do not merge the two sentences.
declared_limits.arm_a_vote_is_choice_only: win runs pando.stemd --backend openai (OpenAIChoiceBackend). Its docstring: 'There is no calibrated probability in that response. Votes are marked neutral.' So arm A answers with a choice and p=0.5/neutral=true on every row. Only choice accuracy is comparable to arm B; a confidence-weighted comparison is impossible for this arm and the tool's accuracy_calibrated column is the one that matters.
declared_limits.latency_is_not_comparable: arm A's milliseconds include LAN transit plus a GPU box; arm B's are in-process on the same mac as the harness. The latency numbers are recorded for the record only and are NOT a verdict input for this run.
declared_limits.interference_declared_up_front: arm A's harness drives the same llama-server that win's own proposer (win-gpu-proposer) uses, 360 sequential requests. It may delay win's proposer for the duration. Done in a single pass, not repeatedly, and not while a win-side experiment is running.
declared_limits.problems_are_internal: heldout4/heldout5 were produced by this project's own pipeline. Author and examinee are the same group. No result here is externally anchored.
